purpose: Separate exact feasible-optimum sensitivity from finite-budget sampler recovery for the 16 frozen Stage70 logical QUBOs before any embedding or hardware execution.

experiment.normalization_rule: Divide every linear, quadratic, and constant coefficient by the maximum absolute linear or quadratic coefficient of its frozen Stage70 model.
experiment.exact_feasible_rule: Enumerate every cardinality-three receptor subset satisfying the integer quality floor and every slack-bit representation; minimize the perturbed expanded BQM energy exactly within this feasible manifold.

noise_screen.quantization_rule: Round each normalized linear and quadratic coefficient independently to the nearest multiple of the stated full-scale step; the constant is not perturbed.
noise_screen.gaussian_rule: Add independent zero-mean Gaussian noise with the stated sigma to every normalized linear and quadratic coefficient; the constant is not perturbed.
noise_screen.interpretation: All levels are dimensionless project sensitivity probes relative to normalized full scale. They are not claimed to represent a particular physical QPU specification.

sampler_calibration_gate.interpretation: This modest gate only confirms that finite-budget software sampling is informative enough to report separately; it is not a hardware-readiness gate.

robustness_gate.interpretation: The reference levels and thresholds are frozen project decision rules, not universal annealer specifications. A pass would authorize only a later embedding study, never a quantum-advantage claim.

interpretation_boundary: Stage71 is a post-hoc software sensitivity analysis on four consumed historical targets. Exact feasible enumeration isolates coefficient-induced optimum changes, while simulated annealing measures only one fixed classical sampling budget. Neither layer establishes physical embedding feasibility, hardware behavior, solver speedup, independent target efficacy, or quantum advantage.
